metadata.theme: Working as a team, reading the evidence, and deciding what is worth the risk
metadata.premise: Captain Odessa Rin and her salvage crew find a drifting ship with no signal, a sealed cargo hold, and a last log note written years after the ship was lost.

items.name: Hook-pole
items.description: A long, light pole with a hook on the end. The tag says it is for high latches.

clues.name: The late log note
clues.description: The Lark's last log note is only four days old. It says: slow air, slow door.

passages.title: A Dark Ship in the Deep
paragraphs: The tug Kestrel was old and noisy. But she was reliable, and she knew the deep road between the stars.
Captain Odessa Rin stood at the front window. Ahead, a dark ship drifted, silent and still.
"That is the Lark," said Tam, the navigator. "She went silent eleven years ago."
Bo, the engineer, tapped a screen. "No signal. No lights. Only a thin hum."
Ivy hugged her bag. This was her first trip. "What if someone is still in there?"
Captain Rin smiled. "Good question. Let us work as a team and find out."

choices.label: Study the Lark's scan with Tam
Link the dock tube with Bo

passages.title: Tam's Star Map
paragraphs: Tam spread her hand-drawn star map on the table. She marked the Lark in red ink.
Ivy leaned in. "Look at that big sail," she said. "It is torn, but it is folded neat."
Fine rain of ice dust tapped the Kestrel's hull. Tap, tap, tap.
On the screen, a round door sat at the back of the Lark. A seal was stuck across it.
"That is the cargo hold," said Tam. "Someone sealed it by hand, on purpose."
Tam looked up. "Now we must choose. Read the ship's log, or look at the hull?"

choices.label: Open the Lark's log with Ivy
Check the hull with Tam

passages.title: The Last Note
paragraphs: Ivy opened the Lark's log. Most of it was old and dull. Days of dust and work.
The last note stood alone at the end. Ivy read it out loud.
"Slow air, slow door. The moths need it. I hope someone comes."
Then Ivy gasped. "The date is only four days old! The Lark went silent eleven years ago."
Tam tapped the screen. "So the Lark was lost. But somebody wrote that note."
Captain Rin nodded. "Bo, dock the tube. We go in as one team."

choices.label: Go with Bo to dock the tube

passages.title: Scratches on the Hull
paragraphs: Tam sent a small camera out along the hull. It hummed past the torn sail.
The hull was not wrecked. It had thin scratches, soft as chalk, and no dents.
"Nothing hit her," said Tam. "The Lark was not smashed. She was left behind."
Then the camera caught a glow. Far inside the dome, a blue light blinked on. Then off.
Ivy let out a breath. "That is a sign. I hope it is a friendly one."
Captain Rin nodded. "Bo, dock the tube. We go in as one team."

choices.label: Go with Bo to dock the tube

passages.title: Through the Tube
paragraphs: Bo slid the long tube from the Kestrel to the Lark. Clunk. It locked on tight.
Ivy followed him through. The tube was thin, and the air smelled of old dust.
Bo hummed as he crawled. He loved small, tight places.
At the end stood a hatch. A tool locker sat beside it. A strip of soft light ran off down a path.

choices.label: Open the tool locker
Follow the lit path

passages.title: The Tool Locker
paragraphs: The locker door stuck, then gave way. Inside lay one long hook-pole, light as a reed.
A tag hung from it. "For high latches. Use it slow."
Bo spun the pole in his hands. "That might help us with a stuck door," he said.
Ivy took the note off the tag. She tucked it in her bag, just in case.

choices.label: Climb through the hatch

passages.title: The Lit Path
paragraphs: Ivy followed the soft strip of light. It glowed like a path of tiny stars.
Bo came close behind her. Their boots made no sound on the thin floor mat.
Thud! Something knocked on a wall, far off. Ivy froze.
Bo grinned. "Old pipes. Old ships talk when they warm up."
The lit path ended at the hatch. Ivy let out a breath and climbed through.

choices.label: Meet the others in the corridor

passages.title: The Quiet Corridor
paragraphs: The whole team met in a long, cool corridor. Captain Rin checked the air. It was safe to breathe.
Two doors stood open. One led to a glass dome. One led to the engine room.
At the far end stood the cargo hold door. It was huge, and shut tight.
"Let us look around before we choose," said Captain Rin.

choices.label: Visit the glass dome with Ivy
Check the engine room with Bo

passages.title: The Glass Dome
paragraphs: The dome was a garden under glass. Dry grey leaves hung from every shelf.
Beyond the glass, a pale moon hung in the deep dark.
In the middle of the dome, one small lamp glowed. A grey moth sat on it. Its wings shone like silver.
"A moth," whispered Ivy. "Alive. After eleven years!"
The moth fluttered up. Something round rolled out from behind a dry plant.

choices.label: Kneel down to see what it is

passages.title: The Engine Room
paragraphs: The engine room was warm. Most lights were dark. Bo ran his hand along a pipe.
"Strange," he said. "Almost all the power is off. But one thin cable stays live."
The cable ran along the floor and out the door, straight toward the cargo hold.
"Someone saved every drop of power for that door," said Bo. "For eleven years."
Then a small light rolled out of the dark and bumped his boot. Bump.

choices.label: Look down at the small light

passages.title: Nib
paragraphs: The bot was no taller than Ivy's knee. A name was painted on its side: Nib.
Nib held up a chalk board and wrote slowly. "The crew left in the boat. I stayed to keep the moths safe."
Ivy knelt down. "You wrote the last note, didn't you?" Nib bobbed up and down.
Then Nib drew three steps on the wall in chalk.
One: cool the lock with the blue tube. Two: turn the valve, slow and slow. Three: lift the door.
Ivy read them twice. The order mattered, she thought.

choices.label: Go with Nib to the cargo door

passages.title: The Cargo Door
paragraphs: The cargo door was tall and grey. Thin silver light leaked from the edge.
Behind it lay a cave of dark, deep and wide.
Bo put his hand on the cold seal. "It hums," he said. "Like it is full of life."
Captain Rin looked at each of them. "This is a risk. We choose it together."

choices.label: Open it slow with the hook-pole and the last log note
choices.lockedHint: Find a long pole and read the last log note first.

choices.label: Ask Nib and the whole team to open it together
Cut the lock fast with Bo's torch
Leave the door shut and take Nib's story home

passages.title: Three Steps
paragraphs: Bo held the hook-pole. Ivy read the last note aloud. "Slow air, slow door."
Nib's chalk steps shone on the wall. One, two, three.
Captain Rin stood beside the door. "The order matters. What do we do first?"

choices.label: Cool the lock with the blue tube first
Lift the door first, to see inside

passages.title: Slow and Slow
paragraphs: Bo cooled the lock with the blue tube. Frost spread over the seal, white and thin.
Tam turned the valve. Air hissed out, slow and soft, like a sigh.
Last, Bo hooked the pole under the latch. The big door lifted, inch by inch.
Nobody breathed. Then silver light poured out over their faces.

choices.label: Step inside

passages.title: A Plan Together
paragraphs: The team stood in a ring. Tam spoke first. "Nib has the steps. We follow them."
Bo took the blue tube and cooled the lock. Tam turned the valve, slow and slow.
Ivy had an idea. "Let me hold the lamp low. The moths may fly to the light."
Together they lifted the door with their hands. A soft rain of silver light fell.
Hundreds of moths drifted out. Each one glowed like a tiny moon.
Nib spun in a happy circle. Now the team had to choose what came next.

choices.label: Carry the moths home in the Kestrel's dome
Tow the whole Lark home, with Nib at the wheel

passages.title: The Moon Garden
paragraphs: Inside, the hold was not a cave of crates. It was a garden of glass shelves.
Hundreds of moths slept on green leaves. They woke, and their wings lit the room like tiny moons.
Nib rolled down the aisle, humming. It had kept them safe for eleven years.
Tam found a second note taped to a shelf. It told where the Lark's crew now lived, safe on a far station.
"We will take them home," said Captain Rin. "The moths, and Nib, and the news."
Ivy smiled at the glowing wings. Reading closely had paid off. Going slow had saved the garden.

passages.title: Moths on the Kestrel
paragraphs: The crew packed the moths into the Kestrel's dome, shelf by shelf.
Nib rolled aboard last. It sat by Ivy's feet, and she did not mind one bit.
The Lark stayed behind, with a bright beacon on her hull. Anyone could find her now.
Tam set the Kestrel's sail to catch the star wind. The old tug rattled and groaned all the way home.
Ivy thought it was the best sound in the world. On the road through the deep, the moths glowed on their shelves.
The team had saved something that mattered.

passages.title: The Long Road Home
paragraphs: Bo locked a thick line from the Kestrel to the Lark. The old tug groaned.
Nib took the Lark's wheel with one small arm. It beeped, proud and steady.
The long road home was slow. The Kestrel puffed and rattled, but she did not give up.
Weeks later, a small boat met them at the dock. Out stepped the Lark's old crew, with happy tears.
Nib held up its chalk board. "I had hope that you would come."
Captain Rin tipped her cap. A salvage crew finds old things. That day, they brought a ship and its friends home.

passages.title: The Door That Stayed Shut
paragraphs: Captain Rin put her hand on the door. "Some risks are not ours to take today," she said.
Ivy looked at Nib. "We will not leave you alone," she said.
Bo fixed a small radio to the wall. Now Nib could call for help any time.
They took the log and the last note back to the Kestrel. Tam marked the Lark on her star map in bright ink.
The door stayed shut, and the moths stayed safe. But the team had a promise to keep.
Next time, they would bring more hope, a good plan, and a long pole.

passages.title: The Door Hisses
paragraphs: The team rushed the lock. The door gave a long hiss, and red lights blinked on.
A cold mist poured into the corridor. Thud, thud, thud went the door as it locked itself tight.
No one was hurt. The Lark was only keeping the moths safe.
"We went too fast," said Captain Rin. "Let us try again with a better plan."
Back on the Kestrel, Tam pinned a new note to the map. Look for steps. Look for a clue. Go slow.
Ivy smiled. "Next time we will do it right." The Lark would wait.

derelict.definition: A ship that was left behind and is drifting with no crew.

salvage.definition: To rescue things from a lost or empty ship so they can be used again.

navigator.definition: The person who plans the route and reads the maps.

engineer.definition: A person who builds, fixes and runs machines.

reliable.definition: Something you can trust to work every time.

corridor.definition: A long, narrow hall inside a building or ship.

cargo.definition: Goods and things that a ship carries.

valve.definition: A part that opens and closes to let air or water flow.

beacon.definition: A bright light or signal that helps others find a place.

fluttered.definition: Flew with quick, light flaps of the wings.
